SOCIAL STUDIES — MOCK EXAM #1
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: SOCIAL STUDIES
TIME ALLOWED: 90 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 80
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Which of these is a cardinal point? (1 mark)
   A. North-west
   B. West
   C. South-west
   D. North-east

2. Which direction lies between south and east? (1 mark)
   A. North-east
   B. North-west
   C. South-east
   D. South-west

3. Which is the correct way to write the in-between point that is between south and west? (1 mark)
   A. West-south
   B. West-south-west
   C. Sowest
   D. South-west

4. Which direction is directly opposite to north? (1 mark)
   A. West
   B. South
   C. North-east
   D. East

5. Why is it useful to know the size of a county? (1 mark)
   A. It tells us the price of food
   B. It tells us the weather
   C. It helps with planning services such as roads and clinics
   D. It tells us what to eat

6. How many counties does Kenya have? (1 mark)
   A. 27
   B. 57
   C. 47
   D. 37

7. On a physical map, what colour is used for water? (1 mark)
   A. Red
   B. Black
   C. Brown
   D. Blue

8. Lake Nakuru is famous for which birds? (1 mark)
   A. Flamingos
   B. Eagles
   C. Ostriches
   D. Owls

9. Which of these places is likely to be coldest in Kenya? (1 mark)
   A. The coast
   B. The slopes of Mount Kenya
   C. A beach
   D. A low dry plain

10. Why does Kenya not have summer and winter like countries far from the equator? (1 mark)
   A. Kenya is too small
   B. Kenya has no sun
   C. Kenya lies on the equator so temperatures change little
   D. Kenya has no rain

11. Why is it dangerous to cross a flooded road? (1 mark)
   A. The road is shorter
   B. Water is always clean
   C. Water may be deep and fast and can hide holes
   D. There is no traffic

12. What is an artefact? (1 mark)
   A. A type of weather
   B. A mountain
   C. An object made and used by people in the past
   D. A river

13. Which of these is a service learning activity at a historic site? (1 mark)
   A. Selling tickets to friends
   B. Building a fire
   C. Sweeping and collecting litter
   D. Painting graffiti

14. What is a museum? (1 mark)
   A. A kind of factory
   B. A building where old objects are kept and shown
   C. A place where crops are grown
   D. A bus stage

15. What does population distribution mean? (1 mark)
   A. How much rain falls
   B. How people are spread out in an area
   C. How many trees are in an area
   D. How tall the mountains are

16. What is population? (1 mark)
   A. The number of animals in a place
   B. The rainfall in a place
   C. The size of a place
   D. The number of people living in a place

17. Which game is played with seeds or stones moved between holes in a board? (1 mark)
   A. Bao
   B. Football
   C. Athletics
   D. Netball

18. Which is a way of conserving water? (1 mark)
   A. Turning off taps after use
   B. Cutting trees near rivers
   C. Leaving taps running
   D. Polluting rivers

19. Which of these is a safe way for a child to take part in economic activities? (1 mark)
   A. Working at night
   B. Working in a quarry
   C. Carrying heavy loads all day
   D. Helping in the school garden

20. What is one problem that industries can cause? (1 mark)
   A. Fewer jobs
   B. Less trade
   C. Pollution
   D. More rain

21. What is a factory? (1 mark)
   A. A hospital
   B. A market
   C. A school
   D. A large building where goods are made with machines

22. In school life, what is a right? (1 mark)
   A. A rule to break
   B. A punishment
   C. Something you are allowed to have or do
   D. A duty you refuse

23. Which of these is a right of a school citizen? (1 mark)
   A. To steal
   B. To bully others
   C. To break rules
   D. To learn in a safe place

24. Which of these is a quality of a good citizen in school? (1 mark)
   A. Laziness
   B. Honesty
   C. Bullying
   D. Cheating

25. What is cyberbullying? (1 mark)
   A. Writing a letter
   B. Reading a book
   C. Using phones or computers to hurt or frighten someone
   D. Playing a computer game

26. When talking about a conflict, which kind of sentence is best? (1 mark)
   A. You are stupid
   B. I will hit you
   C. Everyone hates you
   D. I felt hurt when...

27. What is peace? (1 mark)
   A. A kind of food
   B. A loud noise
   C. A game
   D. Calm and harmony where people live safely and respect each other

28. Which of these promotes peace? (1 mark)
   A. Sharing
   B. Fighting
   C. Bullying
   D. Rumours

29. What is child labour? (1 mark)
   A. Hard or dangerous work that harms a child or stops schooling
   B. Playing sports
   C. Doing homework
   D. Light help at home

30. Who leads the meetings of the assembly of pupils? (1 mark)
   A. The Speaker
   B. The driver
   C. The cook
   D. The gatekeeper

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
31. State three roles of an MCA. (3 marks)

32. Describe how you would make a poster on an economic activity in your county. (4 marks)

33. Give five people who serve your community and say how each helps. (5 marks)

34. Explain why forgiveness is important for peace. (3 marks)

35. A dot map has 1 dot for every 1,000 people. A town has 12 dots and a dry area has 2 dots. How many more people live in the town? Show your working. (3 marks)

36. Describe how your class could showcase its school enterprise project. (5 marks)

37. Draw a weather chart for three days: sunny, rainy, cloudy. Add a key. (3 marks)

38. Name the three main kinds of historic built environments. (3 marks)

39. Write a short motto and explain what it asks pupils to do. (3 marks)

40. Give four instructions to guide a visitor from the school gate to the office using cardinal points. The office is 50 steps north and then 20 steps east of the gate. (4 marks)

41. County A covers 15 grid squares and County B covers 9 grid squares. Which is larger and by how many squares? Show your working. (3 marks)

42. Explain why herding communities live in sparsely populated areas. (3 marks)

43. Explain why early marriage is against the rights of a child. (5 marks)

44. Explain why children with special needs need extra care and respect. (3 marks)
pages.answers:
SOCIAL STUDIES — MOCK EXAM #1 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. B — West
   Only north, east, south and west are cardinal points. The others are in-between points.

2. C — South-east
   South-east is half way between south and east.

3. D — South-west
   We say the north or south word first, so it is south-west.

4. B — South
   North and south are opposite each other on the compass rose.

5. C — It helps with planning services such as roads and clinics
   Planners need to know how much land there is to cover with services.

6. C — 47
   The Constitution of Kenya 2010 created 47 counties.

7. D — Blue
   Blue is used for lakes, rivers and the ocean.

8. A — Flamingos
   Lake Nakuru is well known for flamingos.

9. B — The slopes of Mount Kenya
   High places are colder than low places.

10. C — Kenya lies on the equator so temperatures change little
   Near the equator the temperature stays fairly steady, so rain and altitude decide our seasons.

11. C — Water may be deep and fast and can hide holes
   Floods can carry people and vehicles away.

12. C — An object made and used by people in the past
   Artefacts include tools, pots and clothes.

13. C — Sweeping and collecting litter
   Cleaning up is a way of serving and conserving.

14. B — A building where old objects are kept and shown
   Museums keep artefacts safely and show them to people.

15. B — How people are spread out in an area
   Distribution is about where people live.

16. D — The number of people living in a place
   Population is the number of people in an area.

17. A — Bao
   Bao is a board game with seeds.

18. A — Turning off taps after use
   Saving water helps everyone.

19. D — Helping in the school garden
   Light safe work under supervision is fine.

20. C — Pollution
   Waste from factories can pollute air and water.

21. D — A large building where goods are made with machines
   Factories use machines to make goods.

22. C — Something you are allowed to have or do
   Rights are things we are allowed, such as learning.

23. D — To learn in a safe place
   Learning safely is a right.

24. B — Honesty
   Honesty is a positive quality.

25. C — Using phones or computers to hurt or frighten someone
   Cyberbullying is bullying online.

26. D — I felt hurt when...
   'I' sentences share feelings without blaming.

27. D — Calm and harmony where people live safely and respect each other
   Peace is harmony and safety.

28. A — Sharing
   Sharing builds trust and friendship.

29. A — Hard or dangerous work that harms a child or stops schooling
   Child labour is harmful and illegal.

30. A — The Speaker
   The Speaker leads meetings.

SECTION B
----
31. (3 marks)
   Answer: Represent the ward, make county laws, and approve the budget. Accept checking the governor.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each role.

32. (4 marks)
   Answer: Choose one activity, draw a large picture showing people at work, write a title and two or three facts, and add one way of conserving the resource.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each step.

33. (5 marks)
   Answer: For example: farmer grows food, teacher teaches, nurse treats the sick, driver carries people and goods, trader sells goods.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each person with a correct service.

34. (3 marks)
   Answer: It ends quarrels, it helps friendships to grow again, and it stops anger from continuing.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each reason.

35. (3 marks)
   Answer: 10,000 more people.
   Working / marking points: 12 x 1,000 = 12,000; 2 x 1,000 = 2,000; 12,000 - 2,000 = 10,000. 1 mark for each step.

36. (5 marks)
   Answer: Set up a stall with the goods, display a poster, show records of costs and income, explain each team member's role, and let visitors ask questions and give feedback.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each point.

37. (3 marks)
   Answer: Three boxes with a sun, a cloud with rain lines and a plain cloud, and a key that names each symbol.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for correct symbols, 1 mark for the days, 1 mark for the key.

38. (3 marks)
   Answer: Museums, monuments and cultural centres.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct kind.

39. (3 marks)
   Answer: For example: Work hard, be kind. It asks pupils to study well and treat others with kindness.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for a short motto, 1 mark for meaning, 1 mark for showing action.

40. (4 marks)
   Answer: Start at the gate. Walk 50 steps north. Turn to face east. Walk 20 steps east to the office.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each clear instruction with the right direction.

41. (3 marks)
   Answer: County A is larger by 6 squares.
   Working / marking points: 15 - 9 = 6. 1 mark for choosing A, 1 mark for subtracting, 1 mark for 6 squares.

42. (3 marks)
   Answer: The land is dry, so it cannot support many farms. Herders move with their animals to look for water and grass. So only a few people stay in one place.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each point.

43. (5 marks)
   Answer: It stops a child from going to school. It harms health. It takes away childhood and play. It is against the law because the age of marriage is 18. It limits the child's future.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each valid point.

44. (3 marks)
   Answer: They have the same rights as other children. They may be laughed at or neglected. Including them helps them to learn and be happy.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each point.
